title: PUBG Mobile Metro Royale: Loot Risk and Extraction Planning
summary: Plan Metro Royale runs around gear risk, inventory priorities and exit safety.
intro: Metro Royale runs can involve different stakes than standard battle royale matches. Instead of rushing after the first rare item you see, decide what you can afford to risk and when to leave.

sections.heading: Choose a run objective before deploying
paragraphs: A loot-focused run, a mission-focused run and a high-risk boss attempt require different equipment and teammates. Decide which objective matters most and what would count as success. If your purpose is completing a modest mission, bringing expensive gear into the most contested area may create unnecessary loss exposure. Check the current season's map, available extraction points and mode rules because these can change. Never assume a route from a different chapter remains safe or that every location contains the same enemies.
points: Write down your primary objective and one optional bonus.
Choose equipment that fits the mission rather than showing off its rarity.

sections.heading: Assess gear risk as part of the plan
paragraphs: Before starting, inspect which items can be lost, insured or retained under the current rules. If your best equipment would be difficult to replace, determine whether the possible reward justifies carrying it. Teams should communicate the risk they are accepting rather than assuming every member wants an aggressive encounter. Review consumables and ammunition in relation to the expected route. A less expensive loadout that safely finishes a mission can be more useful than a premium setup that repeatedly fails to extract.
points: Separate necessary supplies from items carried only for convenience.
Avoid relying on outdated insurance or retrieval mechanics.

sections.heading: Manage the backpack while moving
paragraphs: Prioritize items by actual usefulness to the objective and the ability to extract, not only by a visually impressive rarity color. Keep healing and combat essentials accessible. If you become overburdened or spend too long sorting under pressure, the extra loot may undermine your chance of leaving. Decide which lower-priority items you would discard if a better objective item appears. Inventory layouts and search mechanics can change in updates, so learn the current interface in a low-risk run before attempting fast sorting under fire.
points: Agree on team loot priorities before opening a contested area.
Do not stop in an exposed doorway to organize your backpack.

sections.heading: Build a route that includes an exit
paragraphs: Mark an intended extraction location as soon as the mode displays the available options. Plan an alternate route around dangerous corridors or boss areas if your objective is already complete. Monitor available time and your team's health, ammunition and utility. A planned exit can be more valuable than chasing the last rare item deep in the map. When a teammate is injured, reassess the route together instead of making separate decisions that leave someone isolated.
points: Check extraction conditions in the current interface.
Leave enough time for route changes and unexpected resistance.

sections.heading: Review your profit and decisions
paragraphs: After each run, compare the value retained with the supplies and equipment you consumed or lost. Treat these figures as personal planning information, not a guaranteed profit formula. Ask where the team spent unnecessary time, which fights were avoidable and whether the original objective was met. If a new chapter introduces bosses, doors or search mechanics, revisit the plan rather than copying an old farming route. Repeatability comes from adapting risk to the current map and group, not memorizing a single lucky run.
points: Track at least one avoidable risk from each failed run.
Judge a run by what was safely extracted, not by unclaimed loot previews.
